title: Tail budget trimming can leave invalid orphan tool messages in retained history
reasoning: The initial split keeps recent history starting at a USER_QUERY, but _fit_tail_to_target_budget then repeatedly removes the first retained tail message one at a time until the tail fits. That trimming is role-agnostic, so it can remove the user message or assistant tool-call message while retaining a following tool result. The final replacement history is then summary + remaining tail, which may contain tool messages without their required preceding assistant tool_calls. That can violate downstream LLM message contracts or make replayed tool context incoherent.
recommendation: Trim retained tail at conversation-turn/tool-exchange boundaries instead of individual messages. At minimum, when dropping from the tail, drop a whole user turn including assistant tool-call and tool-result sequence, and validate that the replacement history has no orphan tool messages before replacing session history.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests are included, and there is no evidence of a test that constructs oversized recent tool-use history and validates post-compaction message ordering.
suggestedRegressionTest: Create a history with a recent user query, assistant tool_calls, and tool result where the retained tail exceeds target_tokens; after compaction, assert the replacement history either preserves the complete tool-call/result sequence or drops the whole sequence without leaving a leading tool result.
minimumFixScope: CompactionEngine._fit_tail_to_target_budget plus focused validation/tests for retained tail role ordering.
